key_insight: An analytical model links capacitance–frequency measurements to ionic relaxation and predicts the scan-rate window of maximum current–voltage hysteresis in perovskite solar cells.
engineering_relevance: Routine impedance measurements can provide a physically transparent, computationally efficient route to characterizing ion migration and anticipating device hysteresis.
method: Model the transition from low-frequency ion-screened depletion capacitance to high-frequency geometric capacitance, including interlayer effects.
Relate the characteristic transition frequency to the ionic dielectric relaxation time.
Connect capacitance–frequency behavior to scan-rate-dependent current–voltage hysteresis.
evidence_signal: Drift–diffusion simulations agree with analytical predictions across varied ion densities, ion mobilities, transport-layer mobilities, and doping concentrations; experiments confirm the predicted capacitance–hysteresis correlation.
watch_item: Reliable interpretation requires accounting for interlayer effects; the abstract does not specify experimental uncertainty or the model’s applicability limits.
paper_title: Analytical Framework Relating Capacitance-Frequency Measurements and Hysteresis in Perovskite Solar Cells
